summary: Task-selective product UI craft guidance backed by project sources, actions, guards, research, and visual proof.
description: Guides coding agents to produce branded, responsive, accessible, human product interfaces without replacing project tokens, components, Actions, Guards, Evidence, or Readiness.
plainLanguageSummary: Use this for customer-facing pages and product screens that need real design judgment, complete states, human copy, responsive behavior, and visual evidence.

ownership.purpose: Improve the hierarchy, composition, language, responsive behavior, and rendered polish of product interfaces using project-owned design truth.
owns: Human interface writing and content-role economy
Responsive presentation, complete states, and rendered polish review
excludes: Generated, vendored, build, and distribution output
Public marketing narrative and conversion strategy
Business workflow design, deep security review, and data-visualization semantics
overlapRules: Load another pack only when it contributes a distinct flow, component, accessibility, performance, security, or data-interface judgment.
Project tokens, components, terminology, Actions, and Guards remain authoritative over reusable guidance.

modules.title: Hierarchy and brand
modules.summary: Establish user priority, information hierarchy, brand expression, and token-driven composition before decoration.

positiveSignals.summary: The task creates or materially changes hierarchy, layout, brand expression, or reading order on a rendered product surface.
evidence: A product page, screen, dashboard, navigation surface, or layout is Task-owned

negativeSignals.summary: The task has no rendered product-interface surface.
evidence: Owned paths and acceptance remain backend, infrastructure, generated output, or internal documentation

modules.title: Visual composition and polish
modules.summary: Apply disciplined type scale, spacing rhythm, alignment, surface hierarchy, density, component defaults, scroll ownership, and rendered visual review.

positiveSignals.summary: The task materially changes typography, spacing, alignment, surfaces, density, containment, or scroll ownership.
evidence: Owned frontend source changes a rendered page, shell, panel, component composition, or layout token usage

negativeSignals.summary: The task is a mechanical rename or generated-output refresh with no rendered composition change.
evidence: Acceptance requires no visual, responsive, hierarchy, or interaction behavior change

rubricDimensions: surface, border, elevation, and density discipline

modules.title: Responsive behavior and complete states
modules.summary: Adapt interaction and information hierarchy by content constraints while proving loading, empty, error, permission, success, and recovery states.

positiveSignals.summary: The task changes a responsive layout or a surface with loading, empty, error, permission, success, or recovery states.
evidence: Acceptance or owned source names viewport adaptation, navigation, forms, tables, asynchronous state, or recovery

negativeSignals.summary: The task changes no responsive or stateful product behavior.
evidence: The rendered output is fixed, generated, or outside a user workflow

modules.title: React boundaries
modules.summary: Keep client rendering narrow when the bound project uses React or a compatible server-rendering model.

positiveSignals.summary: The task changes a client/server rendering boundary, hydration behavior, or interactive island.
evidence: Owned source uses the bound project's client rendering directive, hydration API, or server-rendered component model

negativeSignals.summary: The task does not use a compatible component rendering boundary.
evidence: Project and Task capabilities contain no client/server component model

modules.title: Human interface writing
modules.summary: Write focused, plain, useful product language that supports decisions, actions, understanding, recovery, inclusion, and user agency.

positiveSignals.summary: The task creates or materially revises labels, actions, guidance, empty states, errors, confirmations, onboarding, or settings language.
evidence: Owned rendered source or acceptance changes user-facing product language

negativeSignals.summary: The changed text is internal code, logs, developer documentation, or generated content rather than interface language.
evidence: No user-facing string or content role is in Task scope

rubricDimensions: plain language, terminology, voice, and contextual tone
page-wide content-role uniqueness and repetition control
action labels, feedback, errors, empty states, and recovery
inclusion, user agency, and interruption discipline

modules.title: Component architecture and naming
modules.summary: Prevent duplicate components and prompt-shaped APIs by making reuse decisions and naming durable semantic responsibilities.

positiveSignals.summary: The task creates, duplicates, renames, extracts, extends, or changes the public API of a reusable UI component.
evidence: Owned paths touch a component catalog, reusable primitive, component export, variant, or shared shell

negativeSignals.summary: The task composes existing components without changing component ownership, naming, or API shape.
evidence: No reusable component or extension point is created or modified

rubricDimensions: component reuse, ownership, API shape, and durable naming

modules.title: Anti-slop visual review
modules.summary: Review rendered evidence for generic visual treatment, repeated copy, token drift, missing states, overflow, and weak interaction hierarchy.

positiveSignals.summary: The task needs closure or review against rendered product-interface evidence.
evidence: Acceptance names polish, review, screenshot, visual proof, responsive proof, or UI closure

negativeSignals.summary: The task has no rendered interface evidence to inspect.
evidence: Owned paths and acceptance contain no browser-rendered product surface

rubricDimensions: surface, border, elevation, and density discipline

failureSignals.summary: Raw color, spacing, radius, or shadow values recur where project tokens exist.
Small interactive behavior repeatedly expands the client-rendered component tree.
Interfaces repeatedly expose technical terms, duplicate headings, vague actions, robotic language, dead ends, or unnecessary explanatory text.
Desktop layouts repeatedly compress or overflow instead of adapting to content and interaction constraints.
Type roles, spacing rhythm, alignment, or density repeatedly obscure the page's primary reading order.
Nested cards, borders, shadows, pills, or competing surfaces repeatedly replace whitespace and hierarchy.
Bounded content, scrolling, navigation state, focus, or persistent controls repeatedly fail in the rendered interface.
Agents repeatedly create components, wrappers, or variants that duplicate an existing semantic role or extension point.
Component, prop, or variant names repeatedly mirror temporary request wording, visual treatment, motion, or feature-local adjectives instead of durable roles.
Shell, breadcrumb, eyebrow, title, description, navigation, and panel copy repeatedly compete for the same language role.
